data.cultural_impact: The name Firoz or Firoj carries the legacy of a brave and victorious warrior, rooted in an ancient Indian culture where valor and triumph were deeply revered. This name embodies the values of strength, resilience, and the triumph of good over evil. In Islamic communities, Firoz is also associated with the legendary Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq, who ruled the Delhi Sultanate in the 14th century and is remembered for his military conquests and architectural achievements.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the name Firoj signifies the inner victories one achieves on the path of personal growth and self-discovery. Just as a warrior triumphs over external forces, so too does a seeker of the spiritual path overcome their internal demons and negative emotions. In Hinduism, the name reaffirms the belief in the indomitable spirit and the inherent power within each individual to seek, grow, and triumph over every challenge. Ultimately, Firoj represents the ultimate conquest – the attainment of inner peace, enlightenment, and a higher state of consciousness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Firoz, meaning victorious in war or conquering in Hindu mythology, symbolizes the inner warrior battling adversities and striving for success. A name that inspires courage, determination, and the will to overcome challenges.

historical_references.reference: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's reign saw the establishment of a new capital city, Firozabad, which became a significant economic and cultural center in medieval India.
historical_references.context: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was the Sultan of Delhi from 1351 to 1388 AD. He is known for establishing Firozabad as his capital city and for his military campaigns and architectural achievements.

historical_references.reference: Firoz Shah was a descendant of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and was born in 1322 AD in the town of Hissar in present-day Haryana, India. He ascended the throne in 1351 AD after his father's death.
historical_references.context: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was a member of the Tughlaq dynasty and was born in present-day India. He became the Sultan of Delhi in 1351 AD after the death of his father.
